title: Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2 claims 'our proposed approach is better than the baseline methods SPL and OGL2P on average' and 'OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC achieves the best average results among all compared approaches, with 0.3% and 0.5% improvements over the second-best method, i.e., RSDA-MSTN.' Table 1 contradicts this: OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC averages 90.1, below its own baseline OGL2P (90.7), below RSDA-MSTN (91.2), and below SPL+JMMD-HSIC (91.0). The claimed +0.9 improvement over OGL2P and +0.3 over RSDA-MSTN on Office-31 are impossible given the printed numbers.

Row arithmetic is impossible: per-task values 96.1 + 95.3 + 77.6 + 98.1 + 77.1 + 99.1 = 543.3, mean 90.55 (rounds to 90.6), but printed Avg is 90.1. All other rows verify exactly (SPL+JMMD-HSIC 91.0, OGL2P 90.7, RSDA-MSTN 91.2). The same configuration is reported as 91.5 in both Table 3 and Table 4 (OGLP+JMMD-HSIC, Office-31, ResNet-50, 6-task average), a cross-table contradiction.

Two invalidating problems: (a) 'D2: ImageCLEF-DA, a constructed dataset synthesized for this study' is provably false — ImageCLEF-DA is the public ImageCLEF 2014 domain-adaptation benchmark (Caltech-256, ImageNet ILSVRC 2012, Pascal VOC, 12 shared categories), confirmed by web search, and Table 7 reports published prior methods' results (RMMD-I TNNLS'23, RSDA-MSTN TPAMI'24, SPL AAAI'20) on this supposedly newly-synthesized dataset, which is impossible. (b) 'For a fair comparison, all hyper-parameters remain consistent' directly contradicts the same paragraph's admission of 'targeted manual tuning per dataset ... to maximize performance, with selective reporting of best results.'

The Introduction states 'the exact elimination of the tensor product remains an open problem, and derivative calculations require further careful analysis beyond the scope of this work,' directly contradicting the Abstract ('we deduce a concise JMMD ... that avoids the tensor-product operator'), Section 3.1 ('the tensor-product operator disappears ... it is easy to obtain the partial derivative with respect to B'), Section 3.5 (explicit derivative 2K^XX(K^J.M^J+delta K^H.M^H)K^XXB), and Appendix B Theorem 3 (complete closed-form proof). The paper simultaneously proves and disclaims its central theoretical contribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix F text vs Table 6 (Office10-Caltech10, DeCAF-6)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix F claims 'OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC achieves the best average results among all compared approaches, obtaining 0.4% ... improvements compared with the second-best method, i.e., OGL2P,' but Table 6 shows OGL2P+Our at 94.3, BELOW OGL2P's 94.6 (a -0.3 change, not +0.4), so on D1 the proposed variant is neither better than its baseline nor best overall.

Row arithmetic inconsistent: the twelve per-task values (89.7, 97.3, 92.8, 95.0, 98.7, 95.3, 94.1, 90.1, 99.5, 93.8, 89.0, 99.2) sum to 1134.5, mean 94.54 (rounds to 94.5), but the printed average is 94.3+/-0.7. Control row SPL+Our verifies exactly (1133.9/12 = 94.5).

Reference [55] gives year 2022 with an anomalous embedded note '(Note: This reference has been adjusted to reflect the last officially verified publication year)'. Web verification (PubMed, DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2021.3093468) shows the paper appeared in IEEE TNNLS vol. 34, no. 1, pp. 264-277, January 2023 — matching the paper's own tables which cite it as TNNLS'23 and contradicting the 'adjusted' 2022 year. The editorial note itself is not legitimate bibliography content.

summary: Exhaustive strict-mode verification of all 54 snippets found 7 high-confidence errors requiring correction, concentrated in the experimental sections. The mathematical core is sound: the concise JMMD/HSIC derivations (Theorems 2-3, Eqs 10-29), the uniformity result (K^1.M^J = M^M, K^2.M^J = sum_c M^{C,c}, K^3.M^J = sum_c M^{WC,c}), the graph-Laplacian weight analysis (Eq 7), and the PSD proofs all verify entry-by-entry (minor non-fatal issues: a missing 1/2 factor in the Laplacian quadratic form of Appendix E, an overstated Representer-theorem statement in Theorem 4, and K^1 written as I_{nxn} in Theorem 1 vs 1_{nxn} in Appendix D). The critical problems are: (1) Table 1's OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC row has an arithmetically impossible average (values imply 90.6, printed 90.1) that also contradicts Tables 3-4 (91.5) and reverses Section 4.2's headline claim of best-in-class results (RSDA-MSTN at 91.2 actually leads); (2) the same reversal recurs in Appendix F vs Table 6, whose OGL2P+Our average is also arithmetically wrong (94.5 computed vs 94.3 printed, and below the 94.6 baseline it claims to beat); (3) Section 4.1 falsely describes the public ImageCLEF-DA benchmark as 'synthesized for this study' while Table 7 shows published baselines evaluated on it, and simultaneously claims fair comparison while admitting per-dataset tuning with selective reporting of best results; (4) the Introduction declares tensor-product elimination 'an open problem beyond the scope of this work' while the Abstract, Method, and Appendix B claim and prove exactly that elimination; (5) reference [55] carries a falsified publication year (2022) with an anomalous 'adjusted' note, contradicting both the verified record (TNNLS Jan 2023) and the paper's own venue labels. Figures could not be verified (image files absent). Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
